sentences.text: Shri Sanjay Kumar Verma - Advocate for the applicants.

Shri Akshay Namdeo - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/
Shri Sankalp Kochar - Advocate for the complainant.

This is the first application under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C filed by the applicants who are
apprehending their arrest in connection with Crime No.668/2022 registered at Police Station-Civil
Lines, District Satna (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420/34 of Ipc and
subsequently added Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of Ipc.
It is the submission of learned counsel for applicants that the applicants are apprehending their
arrest on the basis of registration of offence referred above.
Applicants have been falsely implicated and no case prima- facie is made out in respect of offences under Sections 467, 468, 471 of IPC.
Although, they were added later on but prima facie case hinges upon allegation pertaining to offence punishable under section 420/34 of IPC.

Since offence under Section 420 of IPC comes under the ambit of maximum punishment of 7 years and is therefore covered by the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as recent pronouncement in Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and others reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.

sentences.text: He fairly submits that applicants and their families are ready to repay the liability as per the agreement, provided some interim protection is given.
They undertakes to cooperate in the investigation as well as trial.
The applicants do not bear any criminal record.
Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and on the basis of case diary prayed for dismissal of application.

Learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that applicants have cheated the complainant and after execution of agreement dated 06.10.2017 between mother of the applicant and complainant party, a power of attorney was given by applicant's mother in Smt. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is a case of offence under Sections 467 and 471 of IPC also.
Over the proposal of applicants for settlement, counsel for the complainant submits that if reasonable offer is given by applicants side for settlement then they are ready to settle the matter.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

From the perusal of the case diary and nature of allegations, prima facie it appears that case is covered by the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) because offence is primarily pertaining to allegation in respect of offence under Section 420 of IPC.

Therefore, this Court intends to allow the application and grants interim relief because mediation proceedings are going on with the direction of this Court between other co-accused and complainant, since matter mainly pertains to monetary dispute.

Considering the same, it is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicants shall be released on bail on their furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority/trial Court.
List the case on 10 th May, 2023 along with M.Cr.C. No.13077/2023.

(ANAND PATHAK) JUDGE AT Smt. Anjana Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64458401/
